full_snapshot_s_reason: Recover lost radio state at least every ten seconds.
peer_claim_s_reason: Expire claims from disconnected robots after fifteen seconds.
peer_claim_radius_m_reason: A robot claims a 2.5 m circle around the frontier point it is driving to (about one sweep), so its partner picks somewhere else.
grid_size_m_reason: The grid is centred on the entry point, so it must reach the far side of the house from either door.
cell_m_reason: Resolve walls and door gaps at 10 cm.
depth_stride_reason: Limit depth projection work to every fourth pixel.
obstacle_min_height_m_reason: Exclude the floor and low depth noise.
obstacle_max_height_m_reason: Ignore ceilings above the robot mast.
free_log_odds_reason: One free ray makes an unknown cell traversable.
occupied_log_odds_reason: A measured hit outweighs a free ray.
log_odds_cap_reason: Allow later depth observations to clear old obstacles.
free_threshold_reason: Require evidence of free space before planning through a cell.
occupied_threshold_reason: One measured hit blocks a cell.
robot_radius_m_reason: Body half-width 0.18 m plus a 7 cm margin. 0.4 m closed the 1.0 m front door and every 0.8 to 0.9 m interior door, so the planner could not enter the house.
obstacle_cost_margin_m_reason: Paths pay a cost that rises within 0.6 m beyond the inflated obstacle, so they run down the middle of halls and doorways instead of hugging the inflation edge (the cost map in Kai Nakamura's LiDAR exploration robot).
obstacle_cost_weight_reason: Add a squared clearance cost near obstacles so short routes through jamb edges can lose to wider routes.
stuck_command_mps_reason: Count only sustained forward commands above 15 cm/s, after acceleration.
stuck_measured_mps_reason: Treat forward odometry within 3 cm/s of zero as stalled, including small negative noise.
stuck_window_s_reason: Require 1.2 continuous seconds of commanded travel with negligible measured forward motion.
stuck_strip_depth_m_reason: Mark a 20 cm strip ahead of the body across twice the configured robot radius.
stuck_log_odds_reason: Infer one obstacle hit; three later free depth frames can clear it with the default free update.
stuck_reverse_m_reason: Back up at most 20 cm of estimated travel before turning and replanning.
stuck_reverse_mps_reason: Reverse slowly, clamped to the sensor motion limit.
stuck_reverse_timeout_s_reason: Stop reversing after 2.5 seconds even if reverse odometry also reports no motion.
stuck_turn_deg_reason: Use measured IMU yaw to turn away before retrying a route.
stuck_turn_timeout_s_reason: Bound the turn even if the body cannot rotate.
stuck_repeat_radius_m_reason: Group repeated contacts within 75 cm and exclude frontier goals within that radius of a failed goal.
stuck_repeat_count_reason: Blacklist a goal after three contacts near the same estimated location.
stuck_blacklist_s_reason: Avoid the failed goal area for 30 seconds, then allow a fresh attempt.
ambient_c_reason: Use a neutral prior for cells with no thermal observation.
heat_project_min_c_reason: Project only hot thermal pixels into the heat layer.
fire_c_reason: Treat this temperature and hotter as forbidden.
fire_clearance_m_reason: Keep the requested distance from fire cells.
heat_cost_radius_m_reason: Start increasing path cost before the hard fire margin.
heat_cost_weight_reason: Prefer longer cool paths to paths close to fire.
heat_decay_c_per_s_reason: Keep recently observed fire hot during brief occlusion.
heat_prediction_s_reason: Block cells forecast to cross the fire threshold in the next second.
heat_rise_memory_s_reason: Expire old temperature slopes rather than extrapolate forever.
frame_pair_tolerance_s_reason: Pair thermal and depth only within about one camera period.
frame_max_age_s_reason: Stop driving when geometry, active images, or air samples are stale.
motion_stale_s_reason: Stop integrating a velocity when its sensor stream has stopped.
health_stride_reason: Measure image health on a small grey image.
corner_gradient_reason: Require gradients above sensor noise to count corners.
corner_target_reason: Normalize corner count by forty useful corner patches.
contrast_target_reason: Normalize luminance contrast against a textured scene.
health_threshold_reason: Require more than valid depth alone to trust colour.
health_corner_weight_reason: Give image structure the largest health contribution.
health_contrast_weight_reason: Use luminance variation to detect smoke washout.
health_depth_weight_reason: Include geometry dropout without letting it hide black RGB.
switch_to_thermal_s_reason: Reject short exposure dips before switching to thermal.
switch_to_rgb_s_reason: Require sustained image recovery before switching back.
health_max_gap_s_reason: Reset hysteresis across missing frame stretches.
person_min_c_reason: Allow cooler exposed human skin or clothing.
person_max_c_reason: Reject fire and hot objects above human temperature.
person_min_area_m2_reason: Reject small warm objects and pixel noise.
person_max_area_m2_reason: Reject warm walls and large connected regions.
person_min_pixels_reason: Reject tiny components even if depth implies a large area.
blob_depth_jump_m_reason: Separate warm regions with incompatible depths.
candidate_window_s_reason: Require the repeated observations within one second.
person_confirm_max_range_m_reason: An agent may confirm a survivor only from an inspection within this range; farther, it must approach and look again. rgb_people_eval: per-frame precision 0.93 and range error about 0.24 m up to 4 m, worse beyond; slow-fire run: a confirmation from 6.55 m at the image edge landed 1.55 m from the person, a duplicate scored as false.
survivor_merge_m_reason: Report a person only once within the requested merge radius.
survivor_standoff_m_reason: Approach close enough to inspect without driving into the person.
survivor_stop_min_m_reason: Require a useful viewing distance before confirmation.
survivor_stop_max_m_reason: Do not confirm from across a room.
survivor_face_tolerance_deg_reason: Require the camera to face the person.
agent_arrival_hold_s_reason: After arriving where an agent asked (and facing the point it named), hold still this long for the agent's next order: the recorder asks the agent at most every 4 s after an event, plus one decision period. Run 21: robot A arrived facing a confirmed person within 9 deg, drove to a frontier in the same tick, and when the agent answered 1.1 s later the person was 61 deg off, outside the camera's view.
survivor_dwell_s_reason: Hold a stopped view for three seconds.
survivor_fresh_s_reason: Require recent thermal evidence throughout inspection.
survivor_lost_s_reason: Resume exploration if a candidate disappears.
survivor_stop_speed_mps_reason: Use measured odometry to reject a moving inspection.
standoff_samples_reason: Search several approach directions around a survivor.
replan_s_reason: Refresh paths once per simulation second.
frontier_min_distance_m_reason: Avoid selecting a frontier under the current body.
frontier_gain_weight_reason: Nearest worthwhile frontier first, so an area is finished before moving on; the old 0.04 let a large unknown region 15 m away beat an unseen corner 2 m away.
frontier_information_radius_cells_reason: Count nearby unknown cells as information gain.
lookahead_m_reason: Follow the local path without cutting doorway corners.
goal_tolerance_m_reason: Allow grid quantization when reaching a waypoint.
escape_check_s_reason: How often a searching robot plans its route home to check that the way out is still open.
escape_fire_margin_m_reason: Fire this close to the route home means it is about to close: planned routes already keep fire_clearance_m (1.2 m) away, and the house fire spreads at about 1 m2 per second (agent run 11), so the robot returns while it still can.
heat_cool_after_s_reason: A cell this robot's own thermal camera sees cooler, with no hot reading for this long, takes the cooler value (fire put out or burnt out). Flames flicker within a fraction of a second and keep refreshing their hot reading, so a burning cell stays hot.
heat_emergency_fraction_reason: Below this heat budget, with no exit reachable at the normal fire clearance, the robot takes an emergency exit (2x2 building run: robot A sat beside its entry with the budget at 0).
emergency_fire_clearance_m_reason: Fire clearance for an emergency exit only: the body (0.25 m radius) passes a burning cell with about a quarter metre to spare, never through it.
escape_time_factor_reason: Leave when the fire, at the rate it is closing on the route home, would reach the route's planning clearance before the robot could walk out with this much spare: walking time is route length over open_speed_mps, and turns, doors and slowing near heat make the real walk up to about half as long again. Run 21: the fixed 2 m margin fired 2.4 s before robot B's hallway route closed; it was trapped for 137 s, 89 s above 60 C, 592 C peak.
escape_rate_window_s_reason: The closing rate needs the last three way-out checks spanning at least this long, and is the smaller of their two intervals' rates, so fire seen for the first time nearer the route (one jump) does not read as a fast front (run 22: robot A left at 10 s with fire 6 m from its route before this).
escape_recheck_s_reason: After the way out is lost, wait this long before checking it again, so a route that reopens next to the fire does not start a return that is cut again at once.
escape_ignore_m_reason: The first part of the route, within this distance of the robot, is left to the avoid margins; only fire further along the way out ends the search.
return_arrive_m_reason: A returning robot is back once within this distance of its start. The start is usually an entry doorway, narrower than the planning clearance, so the return path ends up to about half a metre short of it.
open_speed_mps_reason: Use the requested exploration speed in open space.
near_speed_mps_reason: Slow down in doorways and near occupied cells.
near_obstacle_m_reason: Use the slow speed before a narrow passage.
near_cone_deg_reason: Check side clearance as well as the forward ray.
goal_slow_distance_m_reason: Reduce speed before stopping at a goal.
thermal_speed_mps_reason: Limit travel speed while colour is unreliable.
turn_in_place_deg_reason: Turn before translating around a sharp corner.
heading_gain_reason: Close heading errors without requesting excessive yaw.
collision_stop_m_reason: Radius of the near-obstacle slow zone check; emergency limits use the swept body circle (collision_margin_m).
collision_cone_deg_reason: Legacy cone, used only to bound near_cone_deg.
scan_yaw_dps_reason: Inspect unseen directions at a bounded turn rate.
no_frontier_scan_s_reason: Allow a full look around before declaring exploration exhausted.
heat_drain_start_c_reason: Start spending the heat budget above fifty degrees.
heat_drain_per_degree_s_reason: Spend four percent per second at seventy degrees.
heat_recover_per_s_reason: Recover a depleted budget over tens of cool seconds.
heat_retreat_fraction_reason: Retreat before the budget is exhausted.
heat_resume_fraction_reason: Require substantial recovery before exploring again.
retreat_min_distance_m_reason: Choose a cooler location away from the current exposure.
mission_time_limit_s_reason: Bound exploration to the C14 four minute target before returning.
survivor_stop_yaw_dps_reason: Require low measured yaw rate before counting a stationary inspection.
retreat_start_weight_reason: Prefer an equally cool cell nearer the estimated start.
retreat_path_weight_reason: Break cool-target ties with a shorter reachable path.
fixed_grid_origin_reason: Each robot's grid is centred on where it entered; it has no building coordinates.
frontier_gain_cap_cells_reason: Cap the size bonus at 1.5 m^2 of unknown floor so distance decides between worthwhile frontiers.
frontier_min_information_cells_reason: Ignore unknown slivers under 0.1 m^2 (under furniture, wall seams) that cameras cannot resolve and that held robots in place.
visited_radius_m_reason: A reached frontier spot is not chosen again within this radius.
visited_hold_s_reason: How long a reached spot stays set aside; after that the robot may return if unknown floor is still there.
sweep_spacing_m_reason: Sweep once per new area: no second sweep within 3 m.
sweep_repeat_s_reason: A sweep older than this no longer counts for the spacing rule.
sweep_hold_s_reason: Hold each look long enough for several thermal and depth frames (15 Hz).
sweep_yaw_dps_reason: Turn fast enough to keep sweeps short, under the 60 deg/s body limit.
sweep_tolerance_deg_reason: Heading accuracy for each look of the sweep.
area_report_radius_m_reason: Radius for the coverage figure reported after each sweep.
progress_min_cells_reason: 0.4 m^2 of newly mapped floor per window counts as progress.
progress_window_s_reason: Exploring this long without progress means the robot is circling.
progress_skip_radius_m_reason: Frontiers this close to a no-progress spot are set aside.
sweep_max_s_reason: A sweep that has not finished in 12 s ends, so no wall or turn conflict can hold the robot.
collision_escape_s_reason: A collision stop that lasts 3 s without the path clearing becomes a stall: back up, turn, and set the goal aside after repeats.
collision_margin_m_reason: Forward speed is capped so the body can brake to a stop this far short of the first occupied cell its circle would sweep into.
lead_max_m_reason: A robot standing closer to something than the planning clearance steps out through cells the body fits in, up to this far, then plans from the first walkable cell.
agent_avoid_min_radius_m_reason: Smallest keep-out circle an agent's avoid_area may draw: three cells, so it shows on the map. An area that would have to shrink below this to leave the robot outside is refused.
agent_avoid_max_radius_m_reason: Largest keep-out circle: about one room, so one model call cannot close off the house.
scan_yaw_gain_reason: Share of each scan match's heading correction that is applied; position corrections apply in full. Measured on run 13, robot A: the simulated gyro alone stayed within 0.55 deg of true heading over 200 s and 3669 deg of turning, while applying full scan-matched turns gave up to 2.4 deg, because each sweep is matched to a map that has itself turned. Most of that error is matching noise carried forward through the map, which scales with the gain; 0.05 at 10 sweeps per second still pulls the heading to the map within about 2 s, so slow gyro drift stays bounded.
scan_beam_stride_reason: Use every third LiDAR beam for matching (240 of 720).
scan_min_beams_reason: Fewer valid returns than this and the sweep is not matched.
scan_match_range_m_reason: Returns beyond this range are not matched; far returns amplify small angle errors.
scan_sigma_m_reason: Width of the Gaussian that scores how close a beam endpoint lands to a mapped wall.
scan_window_m_reason: Search the corrected position within this many metres of the odometry prediction, per sweep (10 Hz).
scan_step_m_reason: Position step of the correlative search.
scan_window_deg_reason: Search heading within this many degrees of the prediction.
scan_step_deg_reason: Heading step of the correlative search.
scan_min_fit_reason: Mean endpoint score needed before a correction is trusted (0 to 1).
scan_softness_reason: Candidates within a few of these of the best score are averaged, so a featureless corridor keeps the prediction along its axis.
localization_report_s_reason: Log a localization summary (matched sweeps, mean fit, summed correction) this often.
frontier_cluster_max_m_reason: A frontier cluster grows at most this far from its first cell, so a long edge of unsearched floor (common once the LiDAR maps whole rooms) becomes several targets the agent can choose between.
search_requires_ceiling_reason: Robots get no building outline or map. They search only floor where their own camera has seen a ceiling overhead, which keeps them out of the yard and rejects warm shapes seen through windows (Tashon, 2026-10-20: no prior layout knowledge).
ceiling_min_height_m_reason: Depth points this high and up count as ceiling: above door lintels (about 2.1 m) and every obstacle the brain maps (up to 1.9 m).
ceiling_sight_lines_reason: Floor on a known-free straight line from an indoor camera to ceiling it saw is under that ceiling, so it is indoors. The camera sees ceiling only about 4.7 m away, and the 0.6 m ceiling radius alone hid most of small rooms (agent run 14: 454 study cells, where a person lay). A camera in the yard marks nothing, and lines stop at walls and unmapped floor.
ceiling_radius_m_reason: Floor within 0.6 m (walked across free floor) of ceiling evidence is indoors. Evidence sits at least ceiling_wall_margin_m inside the walls, so 0.6 m reaches the floor along inner walls but not yard floor beyond a doorway (run 8: robot B targeted 0.65 m outside its door with 1.5 m).
ceiling_min_hits_reason: A cell needs this many ceiling returns, so one noisy depth pixel does not make the yard indoors.
enclosure_rays_reason: Rays cast from a cell through the robot's own map to test whether it is walled in (every 10 degrees).
enclosure_range_m_reason: A ray that reaches a wall within this distance counts as closed; one that runs this far over floor mapped free counts as open. Longer than the house's rooms and corridors, shorter than the 12 m LiDAR range.
enclosure_min_closed_share_reason: A cell is walled in when at least this share of rays reach a wall. Rays into unmapped space count as neither, so a room partly hidden behind door jambs still qualifies.
frontier_peek_m_reason: Unsearched floor this far past a standable cell, reached only through cells too tight for the body (a gap beside furniture, a strip along a wall), still makes that standable cell a frontier, so the robot goes there and looks in. The strip next to any obstacle is robot_radius_m plus half a cell diagonal (0.32 m) wide, and furniture a person can hide behind is about 0.6 to 0.9 m deep; 1.2 m covers both. Hidden-corner run: a woman behind a desk across a kitchen corner had no standable cell next to her floor, so no frontier was ever offered.
enclosure_max_open_share_reason: And at most this share run out over open mapped ground. Open ground has most of its rays open (or ending in unmapped space, which counts as neither). Through a 1 m open outside door, a room cell 2 m inside sees open ground in about 8 percent of directions and is walled in; cells within about 1.5 m of such a door are not (14 percent at 1 m) and need the ceiling rule.
lidar_open_span_deg_reason: A span of at least this many degrees of neighbouring LiDAR beams with no return is open ground: nothing within the LiDAR's 12 m that way. Smoke loses each pulse on its own, at most half of them (sensors.json smoke_dropout.max), so 60 empty beams in a row by chance has odds under 1e-18. Inside the house the widest empty span is a doorway seen from close up or the far end of the 20 m hallway (about 10 degrees from 2 m inside one end); in the yard it is about 140 degrees. Rays of the enclosure test run on across open ground instead of stopping as unknown (held-out run 2: one long facade plus the person robot B had carried out made the yard walled in).
frames_shared_at_start_reason: No operator pose: each robot maps in its own frame and links frames only from matched LiDAR fingerprints (Tashon, 2026-10-20).
keyframe_spacing_m_reason: Keep a LiDAR keyframe every metre walked.
keyframe_beams_reason: Keyframes keep every other beam (360), 720 bytes on the radio.
keyframe_max_reason: Keyframes kept per robot and per partner.
keyframes_per_message_reason: Each map packet carries the newest unsent keyframe and one older one in turn, so lost ones are resent.
link_shortlist_reason: Own keyframes with the closest ring keys get the full fingerprint comparison.
link_max_candidates_reason: Unconfirmed link candidates kept per partner.
link_max_descriptor_distance_reason: Mean relative range difference (0 to 1) between two keyframes' range profiles below which they may be the same place; the map check then decides.
link_window_m_reason: A candidate is verified by placing the partner's sweep in this map within this distance of the matched keyframe.
link_step_m_reason: Coarse position step of the wide verification search; the per-sweep matcher then refines at 2.5 cm.
link_window_deg_reason: Heading window around each fingerprint turn: two 6 degree sectors either side, so the true turn is inside even when the best shifts straddle it (test: shifts 28 and 32 around a true 30).
link_step_deg_reason: Coarse heading step of the wide search; refined by the per-sweep matcher.
link_min_fit_reason: Mean beam score needed for a verified place match.
link_agree_m_reason: Two matches must give transforms this close in position...
link_agree_deg_reason: ...and in heading before the frames are linked.
link_min_separation_m_reason: The two agreeing matches must come from partner keyframes at least this far apart, so one ambiguous spot cannot link the maps alone.
link_turn_candidates_reason: Verify the three best fingerprint turns in the map, not only the best: rectangular rooms look alike turned 180 degrees.
keyframe_min_return_share_reason: Only keyframes with returns in at least 60 % of directions link maps: out in the yard most beams hit nothing and two empty sweeps look alike (check run 3: a false yard match at fingerprint distance 0.08).
link_unique_shift_m_reason: A verified placement is tested again shifted this far in four directions...
link_unique_ratio_reason: ...and rejected if any shift scores above 85 % of the placement's fit: one straight wall fits anywhere along it.
link_verifications_per_step_reason: At most this many map verifications per brain step, so fingerprint linking cannot stall the 60 Hz loop (check run 3 slowed to 3.6 sim s per minute).
link_coarse_min_fit_reason: The coarse 10 cm / 2 degree search only has to find the neighbourhood; a candidate needs this fit there, then link_min_fit after fine refinement.
link_diagnostics_reason: Log every rejected fingerprint comparison (place_rejected) during the overnight verification runs; turn off for the final demo runs.
ceiling_wall_margin_m_reason: Ceiling evidence counts only on cells at least this far from a mapped wall: wall faces reach the ceiling height band, and their noisy points outside an exterior wall made the yard look roofed (run 6). 0.4 m is under half the narrowest hallway.
person_rgb_min_confidence_reason: YOLO11m (OpenCV 5 dnn) confidence needed for a colour person sighting; the agent's inspect_candidate uses the same 0.5. Measured by rgb_people_eval on 17,816 frames of 9 recordings (4 distinct visible survivor positions, 24 visible episodes): with 2 sightings in 3 s, candidates are 182 true, 1 false over 15 sampling phases (precision 0.995, worst recording 0.980), episode recall 0.48. At 0.6: 171 true, 0 false, recall 0.44. 0.5 kept because the agent inspects every candidate before confirming.
person_rgb_max_range_m_reason: Sightings farther than this are ignored: the box depth gets unreliable and the person is too small to confirm. Measured: per-frame precision at confidence 0.5 is 0.91 at 4 to 6 m and 0.44 beyond 6 m.
person_rgb_sightings_reason: Two colour sightings of one place within person_rgb_window_s make a survivor candidate.
person_rgb_window_s_reason: Window for repeated colour sightings (scans run once per second).
person_rgb_fresh_s_reason: A colour track counts as currently seen for this long after a sighting (thermal tracks use survivor_fresh_s at 15 Hz).
person_rgb_scan_period_s_reason: The recorder runs the colour person detector on each robot's latest frame this often (661 ms per frame on the M5 CPU).
person_floor_clearance_m_reason: A thermal blob's median height must be at least this far above the floor: heated floor near a fire was a main source of false warm shapes (warm_eval).
person_top_max_m_reason: A thermal blob's 95th-percentile height must be under a standing adult's height plus margin; taller warm patches are walls. Not tuned to this scenario's poses (lying, slumped), so a standing person still passes.
see_over_clearance_m_reason: An obstacle whose top (from the live 3D map) is at least this far below the camera can be looked over when choosing where to look from. From a camera at height h the floor behind an object of height o, seen from d metres, is hidden for d*o/(h-o): at h 1.6 m and o up to 1.1 m that is at most 2.2 d, so a person sitting or lying behind a desk (0.75 m) or bed is partly in view over it, while a wardrobe, fridge or wall (1.8 m and up) is not. Hidden-corner run: the desk across the corner counted as a wall.
thermal_lidar_range_fallback_reason: When smoke removes the depth camera's return under a warm thermal pixel, take its range from the LiDAR beam at the same bearing, so thermal can still size a warm blob. Hidden-corner run 2: fluid smoke left 1 % valid depth at times and thermal confirmed nobody while the colour camera was blind too. Limit: the LiDAR plane is 0.45 m up, so it ranges sitting or slumped people but passes over someone lying flat (that blob then sizes too large and is rejected).
carried_person_radius_m_reason: Half the length of an adult lying down (about 1.7 m). A person carried out is set down this far plus a robot's width (2 x robot_radius_m) past the way out, so a robot can pass between the body and the door, and the robot marks a circle of this radius where it set them down as an obstacle in its own map. Hidden-corner run 1: s1 left 5 cm inside the front doorway trapped robot A outside for 156 of 200 s.
search_max_range_m_reason: Floor counts as searched only when the robot's camera saw it from within this distance; farther floor is mapped but stays a search target. It equals person_confirm_max_range_m: a person is confirmed only from an inspection within 4 m (rgb_people_eval: per-frame precision 0.93 up to 4 m, worse beyond), so floor seen from farther has not really been searched. Hidden-corner runs: the depth camera marked floor searched out to its 8 m range, a glance through a doorway counted a room as done, and the robot never went in.
